prerequisites: Linear algebra, multivariate calculus, basic analysis and probability
description: To introduce students to the arsenal of first-order gradient optimization algorithms essential in data science, replacing the classic interior-point methods for large-scale problems. Aim is to understand which algorithm is good for solving what kind of data science problems.

syllabus.title: Introduction
syllabus.body: Data analysis and optimization, least squares, matrix factorization problems, support vector machines, logistic regression, deep learning.

syllabus.title: Foundations of Smooth Optimization
syllabus.body: A taxonomy of solutions to optimization problems, Taylor's theorem, characterizing minima of smooth functions, convex sets and functions, strongly convex functions.

syllabus.title: Descent Methods
syllabus.body: Descent directions, line search, acceptability of step sizes, general minimization algorithm, steepest-descent method and convergence, mirror descent, the KL and PL properties.

syllabus.title: Gradient and Constrained Optimization Methods
syllabus.body: Gradient methods, stochastic gradient, coordinate descent; first-order methods for constrained optimization: optimality conditions, Euclidean projection, projected gradient algorithm, conditional gradient (Frank–Wolfe) method.

syllabus.title: Duality and Algorithms
syllabus.body: Quadratic penalty function, Lagrangians and duality, first-order optimality conditions, strong duality, dual algorithms, dual subgradient, augmented Lagrangian method, Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers.

outcomes: Recognize and formulate convex, nonconvex, and structured optimization problems.
Understand the basic theory and algorithms for solving large-scale problems.
Gain programming experience on numerical implementations.
Use the material in current or future research.
textbooks: Stephen J. Wright and Benjamin Recht, Optimization for Data Analysis, Cambridge University Press, 2022.
Amir Beck, First-Order Methods in Optimization, SIAM, 2017.
